normalized_issues.title: SPEC-00 still forbids direct SPEC-05→SPEC-04 dependency that decoration persistence now requires

merged_from.title: SPEC-00 still models SPEC-05→SPEC-04 as forbidden/indirect even though decoration persistence now requires a direct dependency
Decoration-persistence ownership is still undefined at the architecture seam after the SPEC-07 C1 change

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-00 Module Map lists SPEC-05 Depends On as 'SPEC-01, SPEC-03, SPEC-07' and Seam E explicitly states 'SPEC-05 has no direct assembly reference to SPEC-04; the dependency is purely indirect through SPEC-03's aggregation role.' However, SPEC-07 SDR-07-012 (v1.1.2 C1 fix) now requires SPEC-05 to call SPEC-04's DhfDecorationWriter directly after AppendTurnAsync returns entry_id. The top-level orchestration contract forbids the dependency the new architecture requires.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00 Seam E: 'SPEC-05 has no direct assembly reference to SPEC-04' vs SPEC-07 SDR-07-012: 'SPEC-05 persists this payload via SPEC-04's DhfDecorationWriter after DhfLedger.AppendTurnAsync returns the entry_id.' Also Seam H still says 'SPEC-04's DhfDecorationWriter persists' implying SPEC-07 is the caller.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Update SPEC-00 Module Map to add SPEC-04 to SPEC-05's Depends On list (narrowly scoped to decoration write surface). Add an explicit Seam I or extend Seam E/H to document the SPEC-05→SPEC-04 decoration-persistence path, naming the exact interface (DhfDecorationWriter). Remove stale Seam H language implying SPEC-07 persists directly. Update NetArchTest rules accordingly.

normalized_issues.title: SPEC-07 §0 and SDR-07-006 still claim pipeline success waits for durable citation persistence, contradicting the v1.1.2 C1 ownership shift

merged_from.title: SPEC-07 still states that SPEC-07 pipeline success waits for durable citation persistence, which contradicts the v1.1.2 ownership shift
SPEC-07 still claims pipeline success waits for durable DHF persistence after that responsibility moved to SPEC-05

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-07 §0 says 'The pipeline returns success ONLY after the citation is durably written' and SDR-07-006 says 'The write is awaited on the critical path... pipeline success is reported only after durable persistence.' These normative statements directly contradict Stage 5 which now says 'NOT persisted here — returned to SPEC-05' and SDR-07-012 which moved persistence to SPEC-05. Callers cannot determine whether a PipelineResult means 'payload assembled' or 'citation durably stored.'
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-07 §0 final paragraph: 'The pipeline returns success ONLY after the citation is durably written (§3.1, §8).' vs SPEC-07 §3.1 Stage 5: 'Assemble VocabularyResolutionDecoration payload (NOT persisted here — returned to SPEC-05).'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Rewrite SPEC-07 §0 and SDR-07-006 so SPEC-07 guarantees payload assembly only. Move the durable-write success condition entirely into SPEC-05 contract text. Update ACC-29 description to reflect 'payload correctly assembled' rather than 'durably persisted.'

normalized_issues.title: SPEC-07 StageLatencies still requires DecorationWriteMs and TotalMs that SPEC-07 cannot compute before returning

merged_from.title: SPEC-07 `StageLatencies` still requires `DecorationWriteMs` and `TotalMs` even though SPEC-07 returns before any write occurs
`StageLatencies` still requires `DecorationWriteMs` and `TotalMs` even though SPEC-07 no longer performs the write

normalized_issues.core_problem: The StageLatencies record in SPEC-07 §6.4 has required fields DecorationWriteMs and TotalMs. But Stage 5 now only assembles a payload and returns to SPEC-05 before any write occurs. SPEC-07 cannot populate these fields at the point it returns PipelineResult. The DTO is internally impossible as specified.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-07 §6.4 StageLatencies: 'public required int DecorationWriteMs { get; init; }' and 'public required int TotalMs { get; init; }' vs §3.2 latency table note: 'decoration INSERT is SPEC-05's budget' and Stage 5 row showing 1ms/5ms for in-memory assembly only.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Remove DecorationWriteMs and TotalMs from SPEC-07's StageLatencies record. Define a separate SPEC-05-owned latency envelope that augments the pipeline result after persistence completes. Update §3.2 latency table to reflect SPEC-07-only timing.

normalized_issues.title: GetFeatureTreeInput missing 'Compressed' parameter present in SPEC-02 adapter interface

merged_from.title: GetFeatureTree wire contract still cannot express the adapter's compressed/full feature-tree choice
`GetFeatureTreeInput` still lacks the `Compressed` wire field required by the add-in service contract

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-01 §7.1 defines GetFeatureTreeInput with only IncludeSuppressed. SPEC-02 §3.4 defines ISolidWorksFeatureService.GetFeatureTree(bool includeSuppressed, bool compressed). The orchestrator cannot request compressed vs full feature trees over the wire, so producer and consumer can both follow their local specs and disagree at runtime.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-01 §7.1: 'public record GetFeatureTreeInput : IToolInput { public bool IncludeSuppressed { get; init; } = false; }' vs SPEC-02 §3.4: 'IReadOnlyList<FeatureNode> GetFeatureTree(bool includeSuppressed, bool compressed);'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either add 'public bool Compressed { get; init; } = true;' to SPEC-01 GetFeatureTreeInput with documented semantics and update validators/schema/tests, or remove the compressed parameter from SPEC-02 and define one fixed behavior (e.g., always compressed) documented in both specs.

normalized_issues.title: SPEC-02 oversize screenshot fallback emits FeatureTreeHash='OVERSIZE' sentinel, violating SPEC-01's hash invariant

merged_from.title: SPEC-02 still emits an unsupported `FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE"` sentinel in the oversize path
SPEC-02 still uses an unsupported `FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE"` fallback

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §7.5 specifies that the oversize fallback uses a placeholder StateAfter with FeatureTreeHash='OVERSIZE'. SPEC-01 §8 requires 'The FeatureTreeHash MUST still reflect the hash of the complete (non-truncated) tree so that change detection remains accurate.' The sentinel is not defined in SPEC-01 and directly violates the hash invariant.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §7.5: 'substitutes a placeholder StateAfter (feature tree empty, IsFeatureTreeTruncated = true, FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE")' vs SPEC-01 §8: 'The FeatureTreeHash MUST still reflect the hash of the complete (non-truncated) tree.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Use the real SHA-256 hash of the complete untruncated feature tree even in the oversize placeholder state (the hash can be computed before truncation). Alternatively, formally add 'OVERSIZE' as a supported sentinel to SPEC-01 §8 and update HashCanonicalizer, validators, and all consumers to handle it.

normalized_issues.title: AddinTeardownMessage send path is contradictory: §9.0.2 uses direct socket I/O while §9.0.3 and §9.1.1 claim it goes through SwUiThreadCommandQueue

merged_from.title: The teardown-send threading model is internally contradictory
Planned-disconnect escalation still contradicts the teardown send path

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §9.0.2 TeardownMessageSender pseudocode shows direct WebSocket I/O via '_webSocket.SendAsync(...)'. But §9.0.3 says the 60-second drain is essential because 'if the add-in sends teardown while a COM call is still executing on the UI thread, the teardown send will block behind the COM call on the shared message queue (both go through SwUiThreadCommandQueue).' And §9.1.1 step 3 says 'Do NOT attempt to send AddinTeardownMessage. The send path goes through SwUiThreadCommandQueue.' These are mutually exclusive threading models.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §9.0.2: 'await _webSocket.SendAsync(new ArraySegment<byte>(payload), ...)' vs §9.1.1 step 3: 'Do NOT attempt to send AddinTeardownMessage. The send path goes through SwUiThreadCommandQueue and would block behind the stuck COM call.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Clarify that TeardownMessageSender uses direct WebSocket I/O on a non-UI thread (not through SwUiThreadCommandQueue). Update §9.0.3 and §9.1.1 to remove the false claim that teardown send is UI-thread-queued. The 60-second drain is still needed to avoid sending teardown while a COM call is in-flight (to ensure clean state), but the reason is not queue blocking.

normalized_issues.title: SPEC-02 Day-0 validation step 11 checks DHF session row for closure_reason that SPEC-00 explicitly removed from the schema

merged_from.title: Day-0 validation still tells operators to inspect a DHF closure reason that no longer exists in the schema
Day-0 validation still checks a nonexistent DHF closure-reason field

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §11 Day-0 Validation item 11 says 'confirm the orchestrator's DHF session row shows closure reason explicit_shutdown.' SPEC-00 changelog C3 explicitly states closure reason is 'recorded in orchestrator structured logs (Serilog session_closed event) per SPEC-02 §9.0.4, NOT in the DHF schema.' The validation procedure points to a persistence location the architecture removed.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §11 item 11: 'confirm the orchestrator's DHF session row shows closure reason explicit_shutdown' vs SPEC-00 §2 Seam C: 'Closure REASON (explicit_shutdown, heartbeat_timeout, superseded_session) is recorded in orchestrator structured logs (Serilog session_closed event) per SPEC-02 §9.0.4, NOT in the DHF schema.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Change SPEC-02 §11 item 11 to: (a) verify dhf.sessions.ended_at is set, and (b) verify the Serilog structured log contains a session_closed event with reason=explicit_shutdown. Remove any reference to a DHF row closure_reason field.

normalized_issues.title: ViewerOptions.VocabRawInputAllowed security gate is defined in prose but absent from ViewerOptions class and appsettings configuration

merged_from.title: The viewer raw-input gate is referenced but not present in the documented options or config surface
The viewer's raw-input privacy gate has no tenant-scoped configuration contract

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-06 SDR-06-008 references ViewerOptions.VocabRawInputAllowed and describes per-tenant gating, but the ViewerOptions class in §3 only defines EnableStretchEndpoints, and the §13 configuration example shows no vocabRawInputAllowed key. Additionally, a single global boolean cannot implement per-tenant behavior as described.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-06 §3: 'public sealed class ViewerOptions { public bool EnableStretchEndpoints { get; init; } }' vs SDR-06-008: 'ViewerOptions.VocabRawInputAllowed ... provisioned per-tenant at deployment time as a tenant-level configuration flag.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either: (a) add VocabRawInputAllowed to ViewerOptions as a global flag and explicitly downgrade the per-tenant claim to all-tenants-or-none, or (b) define a tenant-keyed policy source (e.g., Dictionary<string,bool> keyed by tenantId) with a concrete config schema and resolver interface. Update §13 configuration example to include the new key.

normalized_issues.title: Security-event DHF decoration destination is contradictory within SPEC-07

merged_from.title: SPEC-07 still disagrees with itself about whether rejected security events create a DHF decoration

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-07 §3.3 failure modes table has a row 'Bouncer rejects utterance' with 'Decoration Written? Only if security_event=true.' But the note below says 'no DHF decoration is written for rejections — security events route to the restricted audit sink.' And §14 failure taxonomy says security-event rejection => 'No (security events logged, not DHF'd).' Two incompatible rules exist for the same path.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-07 §3.3 table: 'Decoration Written? Only if security_event=true' vs §3.3 note: 'no DHF decoration is written for rejections — security events route to the restricted audit sink per §4.5' vs §14: 'No (security events logged, not DHF'd)'.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Choose one rule and apply it consistently. The §14 and §3.3 note position (audit-sink-only, no DHF decoration for any rejection) is architecturally cleaner and avoids writing attacker-controlled content into the append-only audit chain. Update §3.3 table to 'No' for all rejection rows.

normalized_issues.title: Pre-upgrade HTTP status codes and Retry-After header may not be reliably observable from .NET Framework 4.8 ClientWebSocket

merged_from.title: [speculative] NetFx handshake classification still depends on HTTP upgrade details the spec does not show how to observe

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §6.2 specifies add-in behavior on HTTP 401, HTTP 400, and HTTP 429 with Retry-After header parsing. The add-in targets .NET Framework 4.8 using ClientWebSocket. The spec does not define the mechanism by which the add-in reads upgrade-response status codes and headers from ClientWebSocket.ConnectAsync, which may throw WebSocketException without exposing the HTTP status code cleanly.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §6.2: 'HTTP 429 Too Many Requests — per-IP or per-keyId rate limit exceeded... Add-in backs off per the Retry-After response header' with no specification of how to extract the header from a NetFx ClientWebSocket exception.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Specify the exact NetFx API or exception inspection path used to extract HTTP status codes and headers from failed ConnectAsync calls (e.g., WebSocketException.InnerException as HttpRequestException, or a preflight HTTPS probe). Alternatively, add a fallback classification path when status details are unavailable.

normalized_issues.title: LLM-based bouncer as primary security boundary is architecturally weak for a regulated engineering context

merged_from.title: Brittle dependency on perfect LLM JSON output in bouncer and synthesis despite deterministic pipeline claim

normalized_issues.core_problem: The bouncer is an LLM call with a structured JSON output schema. All bouncer tests use recorded/mocked responses; live-model semantic checks are non-blocking canaries. LLMs are stochastic and subject to prompt drift or model updates. The 'deterministic after bouncer' framing is partially false since the bouncer itself is nondeterministic. For a system targeting regulated medical device design, this is a meaningful risk.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-07 §11.1: 'Live LLM calls are NOT build-breaking... CI uses recorded/mocked Sonnet responses; live-model latency and semantic checks run in a separate scheduled canary that does not gate merges.' SPEC-07 §4.5 acknowledges phonetic evasion as a known gap.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add runtime JSON schema validation with hard rejection on malformed bouncer output (already partially specified via MalformedBouncerOutput path). Consider making at least a subset of bouncer semantic tests build-blocking (e.g., the injection-pattern rejection cases). Document the accepted risk explicitly in SDR-07-003.

normalized_issues.title: Materials corpus licensing is unscoped and may block v1.0 Medtronic delivery

merged_from.title: Unscoped licensing, ETL cost, and maintenance burden for 19k-row materials catalog

normalized_issues.core_problem: CAD_VOCAB_CORPUS.md §2.5 lists 19,295 materials rows as Tier 2 (required for v1.0 Medtronic) from licensed sources (ASTM Compass, SAE). No licensing review, budget, or timeline appears in SPEC-00 §3 Mandatory vs Stretch or SPEC-07 §10. The demo slice is only 22 rows. Phase 3 ETL is estimated at 4 developer-weeks plus licensed data access.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: CAD_VOCAB_CORPUS.md §2.5: 'ASTM Compass (licensed) or ASTM Index' and §6: 'Phase 3 ... ~30,000 rows ... 4 developer-weeks + licensed data access (ASTM Compass, SAE)' vs SPEC-07 §10.1 which lists materials as mandatory for hackathon demo with only 22-row demo slice.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Move full materials catalog to stretch scope or add an explicit licensing review gate to SPEC-00 §5 Review Order. Clarify in SPEC-07 §10 that 'mandatory' means the 22-row demo slice only, not the full 19k-row catalog.

normalized_issues.title: NetFx add-in pseudocode uses Guid.CreateVersion7() which requires .NET 9+ or an unspecified polyfill
normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §9.0.2 TeardownMessageSender pseudocode uses 'Guid.CreateVersion7().ToString()' for MessageId generation. The add-in targets .NET Framework 4.8. Guid.CreateVersion7() is a .NET 9+ API and is not available on .NET Framework 4.8 without a NuGet polyfill. SPEC-01 §18 mentions 'Guid.CreateVersion7() (or equivalent polyfill on target runtimes)' for SPEC-03 but SPEC-02 has no such caveat.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §9.0.2: 'MessageId = Guid.CreateVersion7().ToString()' in code targeting .NET Framework 4.8 vs SPEC-01 §18: 'SPEC-03 allocates CallId values and MUST use Guid.CreateVersion7() (or equivalent polyfill on target runtimes).'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a note in SPEC-02 §9.0.2 specifying the UUIDv7 polyfill NuGet package to use on .NET Framework 4.8 (e.g., UUIDNext or similar), consistent with the polyfill approach mentioned in SPEC-01 §5.
